messages.content: The world reforms. Briar is reading a book in her bedroom. She has no idea of the journey she'll shortly depart for, but she's no doubt holds an aimless goal to see the world nonetheless. A knock on her door. Both her parents are home, but they tend not to bother her.
She stands up and walks towards the door, opening it and peaking out
Her father stands at the door, an envelope in his hand. He doesn't look Briar in the eyes, and waits for her to speak first.
She looks him up and down "Father, is that envelope for me?"

"Yes... Word from your brother. I took the liberty of reading it first, to check for authenticity. You can never be too careful. If it's not in person, words could come from anywhere. It reads like him, and his handwriting hasn't changed much."
Her expression changes to confusion and annoyance but she quickly hides those feelings away "What does the letter say?"

"You can read it for details, but... Well, he's invited you to meet with him, is the long and short of it. I don't like it, personally. You don't have any experience in the real world, so a trip like this... just doesn't seem like a good idea."
Her eyes bright up "Really!? That sounds so fun" she puts her hand out asking for the letter to read it herself

He reluctantly hands it over. "Any number of things could be lurking out there. It's one thing with your brother, he's... different. Never had to worry much about him. You won't have him looking out for you on the way there, though."
"That's fine Father, I can take care of myself"
"Don't forget you still live off of our money, our house, and our food. You haven't shown much initiative in taking care of yourself."

She opens her mouth to complain. She never really had a choice, never allowed to do anything by herself as much as she wanted to. But she quickly closes it and nods. "I understand Father... But I do want to see my brother again, I miss him a lot"
"...Right." He leaves without another word.
She closes the door and pulls on her hair upset. she murmurs to herself as she walks back to her desk to read the letter herself

> To my darling sister,
> 
> I can only hope you forgive me for my lack of contact since departing for the south. Surviving in Newark has kept me busy. Its cutthroat competitive spirit was unfamiliar to me at first, but I have learned to thrive here, in my own way. Eventually, I came to work for the nation itself, and was assigned to a project involving a new type of transportation.
> 
> A new invention, the steam engine, will pull along several carriages along metal tracks over a vast distance. It is said to be a consistent, and convenient method to cross the continent. No longer will our family need to be separated as thoroughly as it has been, due to this advancement. It has hit a snag, however, and thus, I have been prevented from visiting you as soon as I had hoped.
> 
> All I have wished for while I tend to my work has been to see your beautiful smile again. I hope you have been practicing with the violin, as I taught you, refining it into a craft all your own. My yearning for your radiant purity in form of a melody is all that has kept me going in times of difficulty. Thus, I would make a request.
> 
> While I tend to the issue in the construction of this railway, I will be in a small town in the center of Turtima's deserts. If you could spare the trouble to meet me halfway, I would be elated. I have arranged for your transport with the Yondovan workers we have partnered with. They will be in contact with you shortly. I hope you will accept their offer to escort you to Paradise with me.
> 
> With love, Kit

Briar smiles as she reads through the letter, talking to herself "Ohhh the desert, how far away is that?" But her excitement disappears slowly, as she sighs thinking about how much convincing it will take for her parents to let her go.

The world shifts, fading into a new shape. Briar's parents are seated across from her. Her mother speaks. "I don't like it, either. You should just wait for your brother to return home. We can help you cancel the travel arrangements, if you need us to."

Briar played with her hair to the point of pulling it as she tried to not breakdown during this conversation "Mother... I'm going. I don't want to inconvenience my brother after he planned everything out, this is also an opportunity for connections. I could make shows in that town in the future!"

"You've only performed locally so far... to think about expansion to outside of the Yondovan empire before even touring in neighboring cities... you're moving too fast. Your brother has business in that town anyway, he won't be wasting his trip."
"I'm not moving too fast! The opportunity is right here, why should I lose out on it?"
"You're reading too many books. Life isn't a simple path from A to B, you have to... build up to this. The town will still be there in a few decades, won't it?"
"Mother, I'm not disappointing my brother" she says more sternly
"I really want to do this. I haven't asked anything of you two for my entire life, this trip is all I want. I won't bother anymore after I come back"

Her parents make eye contact with one another. They both nod, a look of disappointment in their eyes. Her father decides to join in on the conversation. "Very well. We can hardly force you to stay. We still don't... support this decision, but we're not going to get in your way."
She smiles gently and nods "Thank you mother and father, I'm sorry for the inconvenience" deep down she was so happy she could jump around and scream, but showing that would only cause more problems
"Of course. It's coming a bit late, but your rebellious phase was bound to happen. Once you come back, maybe you'll have returned to your senses. Safety is the priority."
"I will be careful" she kept smiling as her eye started to twitch "I will go prepare my luggage, excuse me"
He makes a motion indicating she's allowed to leave.
She walks away towards her room and starts packing murmuring to herself "I'm leaving this place when I come back..."
The world shifts again. Briar arrives at the convoy. Workers and guards are gathering, preparing to set out on their journey. Bixbite approaches Briar, looking her up and down. "McGregor, right?"
She nods with a smile "Correct! I'm Briar McGregor"

"Right. No field experience, and no history of physical labor. I don't know how your brother smooth-talked us into babysitting you, but just don't die while we're not looking. My liege wouldn't approve."
She nods "No problem! I won't get in your way I promise"

And so, Briar came to leave her nest. Away from the comforting warmth of her city's bosom. Her lungs would fill with the coarse desert sand. The festering filth growing within, poisoning her body and soul. In the blistering heat of the desert sun, all flesh can do is rot.
**End Chapter 10.005**

The world reforms. Mari is in her house, a couple weeks before she would depart for Paradise. Before, in fact, she would learn of its existence. Her mother is in another room, currently not bothering her. Mari is about to leave for one of her walks around Farmton.

Ah, well... I'm grateful for the small blessing of a silent mom. It's a good day, isn't it? Another day. Another walk around this beautiful town. It's all just as meaningful as the last time, and the time before that. I'll find something new to admire, today and tomorrow. I always do. I always do.
I grab a hat to shield my eyes from the sun, then head otuside. My designated master hasn't given me any work today, thankfully, and I'm caught up on my studies. Everything is good.
Everything is peaceful. As it should be. The world moves in its circle.
I consider yelling out a goodbye to Pearl, then think better of it.
She doesn't care where I go. Another thing to be grateful for.

As Mari opens the door to leave, a familiar face meets her. His fist is raised, ready to knock on a door no longer in reach. He flinches backwards from the sudden change in situation, completely thrown off of whatever script he practiced. Either way, Ace is back.
WHAT! My buddy Acilis. My bestie... my wonderful friend. "Ace! Cilly!! Oh my god, you're here! It's been... how are you doing?!" I throw him into a hug.
"Have they been grinding you into dust out there or what?"
His arms move in several different directions before figuring out how to return the hug. His voice seems to suffer from the same disorientation. "Th- Wh- Well- I- Yea- Not- Um... Hi."
"Hi!!!" I release him as an act of mercy.

"Come on, you have to tell me about... how it was out there! You're really back... I mean, we should sit down somewhere nicer. There's a place near here with some shade. Let's go." I grab him by the wrist and start dragging him to my preferred location.
There's a small stone awning I know of a few streets down.
"Oh, yeah! That sounds nice, haha. Town's kinda changed a bit while I was gone. It all moves so, uh, fast, you know? Crazy." He tries to keep pace.
"Oh, no, I really wouldn't say so. Everything still works, doesn't it?"
We arrive. I plop down under the overhang, pulling him down with me.

"So..." I lean in. "It must have been amazing, huh? What did they have you doing? I mean, I know you're not exactly an engineer or anything, but, still... you have to tell me everything, Ace. You must have seen it all... ahhhh...!" I'm beaming at him.

"What kind of equipment do you use? Is it like the stuff we have here? Is it the same, or way more fancy? How much track are you able to put down a day? How do the pieces get put together? Is it, like... ouhhh... come on, Ace!"
I start poking his shoulder repeatedly.

"W-wow, I was hoping you'd be happy, uh, excited to see me, but this is really... Well, the equipment was developed by Newark, it's really not that different, um, but, the scale is impressive... Oh! They do have these, uh, these things. Telegraphs, have you heard of them? Apparently Newark invented them recently, so we're building a line alongside the railway. They're like letters, but they go click and clack from far away, I think? We get instructions from that, sometimes."

"No! No, I've never heard of that... it sounds kind of useless? Like, why would I want clicks and clacks from far away instead of words from far away? But I'm sure there's some amazing reason for it, haha. And, yeah, yeah, I'm excited to see you! Of course I am! It's been... I mean, I'm as happy as ever here, but I still... miss you, y'know? You've always been a part of this town. It feels... wrong to have you gone for so long. Atmospherically? N-not to say that you shouldn't be helping out your family, I mean. I get it! I just, um... oh, so, the tools are bigger? Why is that?"

"Bigger? Uh, no, not bigger, just... there's a lot of them, that's what I meant, I guess. I mean, you gotta have spikes, and rails, and plates... for miles! Each day, you know? I don't know how they make all of these... It feels like it'll never end, ahah... yeah."
"Woahhh... I can't even imagine it, Ace."
I realize with embarrassment that I haven't asked any personal questions, and try to come up with something. "Do you... um... are you making a lot of money?"
He stares at her, dumbfounded. "Am I... supposed to tell you that? I thought it was, um, kind of... I mean, not that I'm accusing you of... Y-yes, I... the pay is good... enough. It's good enough."
I scratch the back of my neck. "Cool."
"I wish I was getting more of that, ehehe... apprenticeship pay, y'know. I'm sure it's nothing compared to what you're raking in."
"I'm... kind of the same, right now, actually. It feels kind of... wrong to be here right now? Like, I should be getting more, I guess, but... they were forced to put us on break..."

"Yeah? Aw, that sucks. Bummer. Real bummer. So, do you want to get something to eat? I know ALL the restaurants around here. Seriously, I have a perfect mental catalogue of them, you would be shocked. There's a great tavern just around the corner? Eh?"

"That'd be great! I've really only been having rations for, well, since I started helping out with the railroad... We stopped in towns occassionally, but... Uh, yes, I'd like the tavern." He stands up.

I hop to my feet and start leading us over to the specific place I have in mind, Rhona's. "What kind of rations? Lots of dried food, right? On a scale of tasting like shit from 1 shit to 10 shit, where would you rank it?" I give him a crooked smile.
"Is... a higher score better... or is it more shit, which is bad...? Um." He follows.
"I don't know. Is it?"

I roll my eyes, but with the smile still on my face. "Jeez, lighten up! You've been acting on edge this whole time, man. I'm not out to get you. The shit tierlist isn't a trick question. I just want to know what you thought about it! You, my friend! Ace! Cilly! Let loose a little! Things are good! You're home!"

"Oh. Yeah, sorry, it's just... hard to adjust? I mean, I talked with people, I was... friendly with my coworkers? But you're really my only, uh, 'friend' friend, you know?" He twiddles his thumbs. "But... for you to be so cheerful, it's... I guess things have been going pretty great back here, huh?"

"Ah, yeah, I'm sure you remember what it's like. Pearl gets up to whatever she gets up to. Dad pays the booze bills. Same old. Honestly, with all the studying I've been doing, I feel like you haven't even been gone for that long! Could've been a week, could've been a year. I mean, I know it hasn't been a week. I've learned a lot. I've learned... so much, really, it's awesome. I feel really proud of myself for it, actually? Like, I've always been on a good wavelength when it comes to understanding how the world keeps itself going, but some of the stuff that guy teaches me..." I try to whistle. It's completely unsuccessful and shameful, but I ignore it and move on. "It's a whole other level. I really feel like I could be out there with you, man! I could be helping! Just, theoretically, I'm saying. I'm good where I am. Things have been pretty great. As great as always. To answer your question."
I reach over and ruffle his hair. "Even better now, though!"

"Ah, ahah, yeah, well... If you're learning that much, uh, you really shouldn't join me? Be out with me, I mean. We don't really need to know much, other than how to, uh, construct things, you know? You're the gifted kid, well, not kid anymore, um... but, yeah, you should find something that uses those skills. I mean, if the opportunity's there..."
"Opportunity, huh? I'm sure it'll come along, yeah. I know it will. Small girl in a small town... it always does, doesn't it?"
"Yeah, maybe that was a... stupid thing to say. But... sometimes opportunity, uh, forces itself? Or, inopportunity, maybe? I-I'm just saying... small towns aren't always secure forever, right?"
"I wasn't being sarcastic, Cilly." I poke him.
"O-oh, but... your mother..." He visibly regrets his words as soon as they come out of his mouth. "N-not that, uh...!"
"Huh?" I don't get what he means.

"Look, Pearl isn't holding me back. She does a lot of things, but getting in my way isn't one of them. She stays in her zone. I've got my own life. If I'm grateful to her for anything, it's that. Don't worry about her! I've got things on track."
"Like a train!"
"You get it? On track?"
"Train track?"
"Oh! Y-yes... I do get it! I got that one, don't worry... It's funny! I thought it was funny."
"Yay!" I consider hugging him again, but it's only been, like, ten minutes since the last one.
Are we at the tavern yet, anyways?

Mari is seated at the tavern. She remembers how she got there, but it doesn't need to actually happen. There's only one conversation here that's actually impactful. The idle chitchat of a lunatic and a puppet.
I wave someone down to take our order.
This part isn't important. Mari is probably going to pressure Ace into picking an option, and he'll fold, because he has no self-confidence or worth as a person.
Do they serve mutton here?
Mari learns there is no mutton served here, making the meal she'll come to have with Ace in several weeks all the more meaningful, unlike this one, which she should stop focusing on.
"So, you haven't told me about the rations. And how shit they are."
"They're really... not that bad. I mean, they're not good? But... um, there's just, a question I've been meaning to ask you."
I poke at my nondescript food as if it's the boy in front of me. "Hm? Yeah? What's up?"

"Why did you believe The Emperor so easily? I mean, you always seemed more... I don't know. You're so curious about the world, and you didn't, well, grow up religious. So, wouldn't it make more sense that there were just... regular explosives planted? And he's just messing with us, saying it was Azalea?"
I look up at him strangely. "What? I've never met the emperor, Acilis. Explosives? Are you messing with me?"
"...Huh?" He stares at Mari for a moment before clearing his throat. "Explosives? N-no, I think they're just going to tear down the buildings."

"O-oh..." I suddenly feel cold. They're just... tearing down people's homes? Their lives? I don't... there's nothing that... I... fuck, fuck. How could he do this? How could he think that this is a good idea? And how could... how could Ace... how could my Cilly just go along with it? Bring it up like it's nothing?
I shake my hands out a few times. "Ace, I don't understand. Why can't they go around?"

"Well... orders come from the higher-ups, you know? ...Budget, maybe? A straight line takes less material... Haha, but I guess putting the project on hiatus probably, well, loses more money... I don't really get it, either, but... work's work..."

"Yeah. Yeah, you're right. Work's work, huh?" It takes me a moment to adjust, but... I see him in a new light for the first time. This isn't the same person who left me, is it? This is a different man. I've been treating him like nothing has changed, but that's not exactly true. I see it now. He has muscles in places he didn't before... a stockier build, skin freckled and mottled by the sun. He's moved up in life, and I've stayed down here. I guess he doesn't see it anymore, does he? What it all means. He did, once. He knew what it would mean to tear down a person's life, to have power over somebody and choose to fall into greed and convenience anyways, to force them to fend for themself. He should know. But this... this isn't his fault. And it's not inevitable, either. My moment of clarity finally builds to its foregone conclusion.
"Hey, Ace... I know it's on pause right now, but... do you think I was right before? When I said that I could be useful out there? I know it's not what I'm training for, but... a job's a job, right?"
I smile warmly.
For the first time today, Ace returns her smile. "Y-yeah! I don't know if they're hiring... but maybe we could work something out. You know, uh, I was honestly, kind of hoping you'd ask!"
**End Chapter 10.005**

The world reforms. Atie is en route to the train, currently stopped at a station within Newark. After a successful interview process, she was selected as assistant to the engineer. Her superior, Theo McGregor, thought it prudent to introduce the staff to one another, so she was called here a few days before the vessel is set to depart on its long journey.
"Hello. I'm Atie Alcule." Atie whispers to herself, making sure she can say it without her voice failing.
The air fails to muster a response. She eventually reaches the station. Theo welcomes her with a wave and a grin, standing next to two women Atie hasn't seen before.

"." Atie's voice fails. She desperately tries again. "H-Hello. I'm Atie Alcule." She then realizes Theo probably already recognized her, but the women might not have. She awaits a response in order to learn who they are.
The larger woman holds out her hand, offering a handshake. "Nice to meetcha. I'm Val. Well, Valerie, but you can call me Val, since we'll be working together and all."
"Nice to meet you, Val."
"Mhm... Not one for handshakes, then?" She pulls her hand back some, trying to gauge whether it's going to be met with Atie's.
Atie does shake her hand, even if unintentionally late.

The other woman watches this, deciding it's her turn to speak once the handshake is finished. "Rhea Van Halen. You may have heard of me, but I have no interest in appeasing fangirls. If you are to be my assistant, I require rationality, is that understood?"
"Yes." Atie senses the more serious tone, though the reason for it is not clear.

"Good." She's satisfied with that.

Val rolls her eyes. "Forgive her, she goes through assistants like this hunk of metal goes through its fuel. I think they all kinda blend together for her."
"I see."

"They are all the same. Ruled by emotions. There is nothing to be learned by such creatures. I don't need distractions from my work." Rhea stares at the train. She barely seems like she's talking to anyone now.

Theo glances around casually, looking for something, or someone.

Atie has no clue what Rhea is talking about or what prompted it. Is Rhea mad specifically at her? How can she become different and lose her emotions to avoid distracting Rhea? Atie blinks, leaving this train of thought behind, and looks at Theo again.

"Ah, here we are." Theo waves again, not to Atie, but to a new arrival.

"H-h-hi everyone! I-i-it's a pleasure to, uh, to make, to be of, acquaintance to, uh... W-wait... Atie!?" A familiar voice, a familiar face. Penny Welsh arrives on the platform, seeing Atie again for the first time since their studies together.
"Penny! Hi!"
"I d-didn't know... we'd, um, we'd be- you'd be here! How have y-you... been??" She sidles into the group circle.
"I've been fine. It's good to see you here."
"Oh! Good to see, m-me, yeah, I'm good, to see. What are you- um, j-job? Your job here? What are you d-doing? For a job?"
"I'm supposed to assist the engineer."
"O-oh..." Her face darkens, yet somehow reddens at the same time. "W-well... that's good! I'm the, well, I-I'm the cook. I'm the cook, for the train! Cooking m-meals. That's what I'm cooking."

"Oh! That's cool!"
Penny might be a bit jealous. However, Atie is still focused on being the engineer herself one day, so she doesn't quite see it the same way. She simply thinks it is cool that Penny is the cook, and immediately imagines her making a mess in the kitchen. She then remembers the people from the train, and turns back towards them.

Theo clasps his hands together. "Yes, well, I'm sure the fine talents of Newark will serve and assist as appropriate. Next, allow me to provide a tour of the vessel. Come, then." He motions for the group to follow him into the train.
Atie follows

Her legs are glued in place. More accurately, she *feels* like her legs are glued in place. They move, but not to her command. Her body continues, moving ahead of her point of view. Everything feels stiff, she can only stare forward and think, while the 'Atie Alcule' in front of her makes her way into the train.
She tries to process the scene, but fails. There is no possible explanation for what's going on. Her mental state is filled with only panic, as if waking up from a dream that has suddenly collapsed.

Atie's body stands in the train, discussing something with the group. She can't hear them, she's too far away, even though her body is right next to everyone else. There's someone else in the train. Someone who shouldn't be there. A man with silky, pure white hair. She can see him through the window. He stands behind her body, whispering into her ear. She can't hear him. She won't remember what he's saying.
[What am I?]

The train begins to move. It shouldn't be moving today, but it does anyway. Slowly, then gaining speed. Atie's body is whisked away along with her coworkers, but the man stays. He's anchored into place, sliding along the floor of the train, passing between cars. His unblemished white robes flow in the wind of the moving vehicle. He turns to look at Atie. At her point of view.

"How does it feel?"
[What is "it"?]

"The river follows the shortest path. The grooves carved out by previous rainfall. You created a mold of your life, and now it will be filled. It doesn't really matter who fills it, does it? You never gave me that courtesy, after all."
[Take me back!]

"You blame me, then. Typical. You really don't know who your enemy is, do you? You just do as you're told, ignorant of the blood your achievements will be built on. All the way until it's yours. That's when you start caring."
[What did I do? What are you doing? Why don't you tell me anything?]

"Neither of us really *do* anything. History is carved around us. I just expand to fill the space, it's what I've always done to survive. You, on the other hand, have just been replaced. My condolences."
[No, that's just more nonsense! What's going to happen to me?]
"For now, you'll wake up like this didn't even happen. It will be the next day, and you'll have your body. As far as it matters, it'll be like you actually still exist. Enjoy it, while it lasts."
**End Chapter 10.005**
The world reforms. Alonsa arrives at the museum for a day of curation and study of the items held within. It won't open to the public for a few hours, so only employees are inside right now.
She walks inside!
Todays a great day to have a great day!
Tanner is visible from the foyer of the museum, arranging a new exhibit on fossils of extinct birds, including samples that arrived recently.
She goes to the birds and inspects them.
Birds are a little boring... they don't change much over the centuries, and their bones don't tell interesting stories. But all fossils have something fascinating about them.

Most of the fossils on display are pretty small. The largest is positioned in the center, a reconstruction of a bird about 45 cm in length. As Tanner arranges the items, he glances to Alonsa. "Ah, good morning! I just finished verifying the authenticity of this sample. Beautiful, isn't it?"
"Morning!"
"It's, uhhhhh..."
"How old is that bird?"
"Judging by where it was discovered, likely hundreds of thousands of years."
She didn't want to say it, but that's kinda young, for a fossil.
"I'm impressed it was able to solidify so well in that time."
"Fossilization is truly an interesting process. We could learn a lot from it."
"Yeah..."
It's no anthropology, that's for sure.
"What is your opinion on the beak shape?" The fossil has a very long, pointed, and narrow beak relative to the size of the bird's head. It's almost akin to a sword, using the head as a hilt.
"Long thin beaks like that are common among birds that specialize in foraging for bugs."
"Still, it's not super common to see one so big."
"It looks sharp, almost like the beak of a hawk or something."

"Yes, I theorized the same. An ornithologist I spoke with brought up a different theory, though. They believe this beak would serve well in hunting for aquatic prey. It would allow them to dive in with little resistance from air or water. A quick and deadly strike to capture its prey."
"Interesting."
"Wouldn't something similar to a pelican be better suited?"
"Scooping the prey out of the water rather then spearing them through."
"No wonder they were naturally selected out, then."

"Hah. Yes, well, there's never only one way to cook an egg. I don't bring this up because I believe it's a brilliant adaptation for survival, I'm simply appreciating the implications it could have. The same shape, the same principle, could be applied on modern day transportation, pushing us beyond the limits of our current speeds. A machine has no need to catch its prey."
"Transporation via... diving into the water?"

"I'm speaking of the lowered wind resistance. It's... Hm, well, it's a bit of a secret, so don't tell anyone I let you know, but Newark's government is developing something. It's a faster form of transportation, a long series of boxes on wheels. I don't really know how it works, but... it's quite marvelous."
"How do they plan on... getting the boxes to move?"
"I'm assuming if they were just camel-drawn or something it wouldn't be interesting."
"It's... powered by fire, I think? Blazing coal causes its wheels to spin on their own... somehow. Like I said, I don't really know too much about that. I haven't seen schematics, or anything."
"...Interesting."
"Building that would require a lot of infastructure, so it's probably gonna be good for the economy."

"And imagine the increase in trade! I can hardly wait for its completion." He sighs, and droops his head. "I just wish everyone was as excited. Some backwater desert folk are delaying it. Those rails are much more important to progress than their little town!"
"Where exactly... is this being built?"

"Straight across Turtima, end to end. Right now they've gotten about halfway. They're trying to build in... ah... Paradise, I believe. That's the town that's refused to leave. Our government's offered relocation to new housing and everything, what a stubborn bunch."
"That's..."
"Wait, hold on. What does the construction involve? It's not going to... Are they going to tear down the town?"

"Maybe not all of it, anything on the edge could be untouched, but given its age it might be safer to just take down everything. A flat, open area is needed. They might even build a stop there, in addition to the track."
"A flat open area??!!"
"They can't do that. They..."
"Do you know how much archeological research that can be done in that town?"
"We could learn so much about the history of Newark... the history of Turtima as a whole..."
"Destroying that place... even if its in the name of 'progress', it'll set us back hundreds of years! We'd never know the truth about our past!"
"Something has to be done about this. Call whatever friends you have in the city, tell them to redirect it somewhere else. No, but... that whole region is filled with ruins..."
"Ugh, why couldn't they build it on the coast..."

"The diameter is a shorter trip than the circumference, I suppose. I take no delight in destruction of history, but we have to weigh the benefits here. We could spend our whole lives searching for discoveries as impactful as this new vehicle and find nothing. I research history to expediate progress, not to get in its way."
“No! I can’t accept that.”
“What is ‘progress’ anyway? What are we progressing into? It’s a nonsense philosophy.”

“If we don’t know the past, then we can’t decide where we need to go for the future! And if we’re sacrificing the past in the name of “progress” then that isn’t… we’re not building towards a future, we’re just building towards an abstract nothing!”

"I hardly agree. We're building towards a perfected society, we just need to follow where inventions and discoveries take us. Ideally, we'll have no need for the past once-" A squelching sound. Blood begins to drip from one of Tanner's eyes. He touches it with his hand, and stares at the blood on his fingertip in confusion. "That's... strange. I don't remember... that happening..."
"T-Tanner!?"
"What's happening?"
